# Sirach Chapter 45 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 45 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 45 covers three figures: Moses (vv. 1–5), Aaron (vv. 6–22), and Phinehas (vv. 23–26). Aaron dominates, with a detailed description of the high-priestly vestments drawn from Exodus 28–29 and Leviticus. These vestment descriptions require precision — they should echo the exodus passages without being a free paraphrase.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 1: "From him" (EMET) vs. "From Jacob" (LOGOS) — the antecedent is Jacob from the previous chapter. SOPHIA supplies "Jacob" for clarity.
- v. 5: "thick cloud" vs. "dark cloud" — Greek gnophon = thick darkness, gloom. "Thick darkness" or "dark cloud" better than "thick cloud." SOPHIA adopts "dark cloud."
- v. 8: "ephod" — preserve untranslated as a recognized liturgical term.
- vv. 10–12: The vestment catalog. Preserve "Urim and Thummim" untranslated (both are recognized terms). Maintain the list structure of vv. 10–11 with "with... with... with."
- v. 12: "engraved with the seal of holiness" — EMET's phrase is more literal; this is the inscription "Holy to the LORD" on the golden plate (Ex. 28:36).
- v. 23: "zealous in the fear of the Lord" — Phinehas's zeal is critical; all agents preserve it.
- v. 25: The Aaron/David covenant parallel is theologically significant; the two covenants (Davidic and Aaronide) are being equated in importance.

---

**45:1** From Jacob he brought forth a man who found favor in the sight of all, beloved by God and men alike — Moses, whose memory is blessed.

**45:2** He made him equal in glory to the holy ones and made him great, so that his enemies stood in awesome fear of him.

**45:3** By his word he made signs cease; he glorified him in the presence of kings, gave him commandments for his people, and showed him a portion of his glory.

**45:4** He sanctified him through faithfulness and meekness; he chose him from among all humanity.

**45:5** He made him hear his voice and led him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments face to face — the law of life and knowledge — so that he might teach Jacob the covenant and enlighten Israel with his decrees.

**45:6** He exalted Aaron, a holy man like him, his brother, of the tribe of Levi.

**45:7** He made an everlasting covenant with him and gave him the priesthood of the people; he adorned him with splendor and girded him with a glorious robe.

**45:8** He clothed him in perfect glory and strengthened him with the symbols of authority: the linen breeches, the long robe, and the ephod.

**45:9** He encircled him with pomegranates and with many golden bells all around, to sound at every step he took, to make their music heard in the temple as a reminder to his people.

**45:10** With the sacred vestment of gold and blue and purple, the work of a skilled embroiderer; with the oracle of judgment, the Urim and Thummim;

**45:11** with twisted scarlet, the work of a craftsman; with precious stones engraved like seals in settings of gold, the work of a jeweler — a memorial according to the number of the tribes of Israel;

**45:12** with a golden crown upon his turban, engraved with the seal of holiness, a glorious distinction, a work of skill, a delight for the eyes, beautiful beyond measure.

**45:13** Before him there were no such things. No outsider ever wore them; only his sons, and his descendants forever.

**45:14** His sacrifices were wholly burned twice each day, continually.

**45:15** Moses ordained him and anointed him with holy oil; it was an everlasting covenant for him and his descendants as long as the heavens endure, to serve as priest and to bless the people and praise him by name.

**45:16** He chose him from among all the living to offer sacrifice to the Lord, incense and a pleasing aroma as a memorial offering, to make atonement for the people.

**45:17** Through his commandments he gave him authority in statutes and judgments, to teach Jacob his testimonies and to enlighten Israel in his law.

**45:18** Outsiders plotted against him and envied him in the wilderness — the followers of Dathan and Abiram and the company of Korah, in their fury and rage.

**45:19** The Lord saw it and was not pleased, and they were consumed in the heat of his anger; he worked wonders against them and destroyed them in blazing fire.

**45:20** He magnified the glory of Aaron and gave him his inheritance; he allotted him the firstfruits of the produce.

**45:21** He prepared bread for them in abundance; they eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to Aaron and his descendants.

**45:22** But in the land of the people he has no inheritance, and he has no portion among the people; for the Lord himself is his portion and his inheritance.

**45:23** Phinehas son of Eleazar is third in glory, zealous in the fear of the Lord; he stood fast when the people turned away, with the noble courage of his soul, and made atonement for Israel.

**45:24** Therefore a covenant of peace was established with him, that he should lead the sanctuary and his people, so that he and his descendants should hold the dignity of the priesthood forever.

**45:25** A covenant was also established with David son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah: the royal inheritance passes from son to son alone; so the heritage of Aaron is for his descendants alone.

**45:26** May God now grant you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, so that their prosperity may not perish and their glory may endure for all their generations.
